claims.assertion: Za’el argues that moral relativism and excessive tolerance can let more aggressive, authoritarian people impose rules on peaceful others.
claims.speaker: Za’el de Erra

claims.assertion: In his game analogy, the rule-setter determines who wins; powerful actors can similarly define or manipulate ethical rules and perceived reality.
claims.speaker: Za’el de Erra

claims.assertion: He advises keeping one’s ethics and empathy while refusing passivity toward abuse or allowing others to control one’s circumstances.
claims.speaker: Za’el de Erra

claims.assertion: He urges examining multiple sides and recognizing wrongdoing without treating it as self-defining, then acting nobly while resisting harm.
claims.speaker: Za’el de Erra
